mainTopic: מלקות for a לאו שקדמו עשה, and why an אונס who divorces is not lashed
overview: Right before this, רבי יוחנן was quoted as ruling that one gets מלקות for a לאו that has an עשה before it (לאו שקדמו עשה). When asked, he denies saying it. רבה swears that he did, and shows the rule in a פסוק and a משנה. The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן was bothered by a ברייתא: an אונס who divorced the girl, if he is a ישראל, takes her back and gets no lashes. עולא tries to show that the אונס's עשה really means 'if he divorced her, he must remarry her,' using קל וחומר and 'אם אינו ענין' with the case of מוציא שם רע. Each attempt is refuted. In the end רבא, and רבי יוחנן as reported by רבין, learn it from 'כל ימיו': all his days he must take her back. רב פפא then asks why a לאו with an extra עשה should still get lashes, and רבא explains that only an עשה that comes to fix the לאו removes lashes. The amud ends by asking how רבא's answer fits the view of 'קיימו ולא קיימו,' and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is asked if he said it and denies it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is asked whether he really said the rule about לאו שקדמו עשה, and he answers no.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי יוחנן: Did you say this rule? He told them: No.
steps.whatsHappening: Others check with רבי יוחנן whether the rule quoted in his name is really his, and he says he did not say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in question is that someone gets lashes for a לאו when an עשה comes before it. By saying 'no', רבי יוחנן seems to be backing away from this rule. That sets up the next two steps: someone insists he did say it, and then the גמרא asks why he backed away.

phrases.english: They said to him: Did you say [this]?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יוחנן, and 'this' is his rule that you get lashes for a לאו when an עשה comes before it.

phrases.english: He said to them: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָמַרְתָּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks whether the rule quoted just before in רבי יוחנן's name is really his.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי יוחנן really rule that one gets lashes for a לאו שקדמו עשה?

steps.title: רבה swears he said it and brings a פסוק and a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה swears that רבי יוחנן did say the rule. He adds that it is written in the Torah (the camp of impurity) and taught in a משנה (one who enters the מקדש impure).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: By God! He said it. And it is written in the Torah, and we learned it in a משנה. It is written: 'They shall send out of the camp...' and 'they shall not make their camp impure.' And we learned in the משנה: one who comes into the מקדש while impure (gets lashes).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה swears that רבי יוחנן really did say the rule. He then backs up the rule with a פסוק and a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives an עשה to send impure people out of the camp. That is followed by a לאו, 'they shall not make their camp impure.' The משנה lists 'one who enters the מקדש impure' among those who get lashes, so here is a לאו with an עשה before it, and lashes are still given.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule is not just one sage's opinion. It has a clear source in the Torah and in a משנה, which makes רבי יוחנן's backing away even more puzzling.

phrases.english: Rabba said: By God!
phrases.notes: He is swearing that he really heard רבי יוחנן say it.

phrases.english: He said it, and it is written, and we learned it:
It is written: "And they shall send out of the camp, etc."
"And they shall not make their camp impure."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:3. This is the לאו, which comes after the עשה.

phrases.english: We learned: one who comes into the Temple impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הָאֱלֹהִים! אַמְרַהּ, וּכְתִיבָא וּתְנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יוחנן's denial and gives sources for the rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one gets lashes for a לאו שקדמו עשה (and that רבי יוחנן said it).
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 5:2-3 (send out of the camp / do not make the camp impure), together with the משנה about one who enters the מקדש impure.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן back away?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule has such strong sources, why did רבי יוחנן deny saying it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then what is the reason he backed away from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן would deny a rule that has a פסוק and a משנה behind it. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts רבה's claim that the rule is solid. So there must be some other source that bothered רבי יוחנן and made him pull back.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted / took back his words

phrases.english: Rather, what is the reason
that he retracted it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי טַעְמָא קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבה proved the rule is well grounded, the גמרא asks what made רבי יוחנן deny it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source caused רבי יוחנן to retract his rule?

steps.title: The case of the rapist who divorced bothered him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן backed away because of a ברייתא about an אונס who divorced. A ישראל takes her back and gets no lashes; a כהן gets lashes and does not take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the case of an אונס was hard for him. As a ברייתא teaches: an אונס who divorced his wife — if he is a ישראל, he takes her back and does not get lashes; if he is a כהן, he gets lashes and does not take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a ברייתא about an אונס made רבי יוחנן back away. It quotes that ברייתא in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says an אונס must marry the girl ('ולו תהיה לאשה'), and also that he may never send her away. A ישראל who divorces her just remarries her and gets no lashes. A כהן cannot remarry a divorcee, so he cannot fix it and he gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a young unmarried girl; the Torah requires him to marry her

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the כהן gets lashes because he is a כהן. Both men broke the same לאו by divorcing. The difference is that the ישראל can fix it by taking her back, and the כהן cannot, because a כהן may not marry a divorcee.

phrases.english: Because the case of a rapist was difficult for him.
As it was taught: a rapist who divorced [her],
if he is a Yisrael,
he takes her back and does not get lashes.
If he is a kohen,
he gets lashes and does not take her back.
phrases.notes: A כהן is not allowed to marry a divorced woman, so he cannot take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ אוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by bringing the ברייתא of אונס.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא about an אונס who divorced made רבי יוחנן retract.

steps.title: Why isn't the Yisrael rapist flogged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the problem: the אונס's לאו has an עשה before it, so by the rule he should get lashes, yet the ברייתא says a ישראל does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is a ישראל, he takes her back and gets no lashes. Why? This is a לאו that has an עשה before it, so let him get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly why the אונס case is hard for רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עשה 'ולו תהיה לאשה' comes before the לאו 'לא יוכל שלחה'. By רבי יוחנן's rule, a לאו שקדמו עשה gets lashes, so the ישראל should get lashes. The ברייתא says he does not, which seems to go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that has a positive command coming before it

phrases.english: If he is a Yisrael,
he takes her back and does not get lashes — why?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁקְּדָמוֹ עֲשֵׂה הוּא, וְלִילְקֵי!
phrases.english: It is a prohibition that has a positive command before it — so let him get lashes!
phrases.notes: In דברים 22:29, 'and she shall be his wife' comes before 'he may not send her away'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁקְּדָמוֹ עֲשֵׂה הוּא, וְלִילְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא of step 4 conflicts with the rule of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a לאו שקדמו עשה gets lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אונס's לאו has an עשה before it, yet the ברייתא says a Yisrael gets no lashes. That suggests a לאו שקדמו עשה does not get lashes.

steps.title: עולא: the words 'she shall be his wife' are extra
steps.stepSummary: עולא starts his answer. The words 'ולו תהיה לאשה' are not needed for the basic duty to marry, because that could be learned through a קל וחומר from מוציא שם רע. So they must be teaching something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The Torah did not need to say 'she shall be his wife' about an אונס; we could learn it from a מוציא שם רע. If a מוציא שם רע, who did no action, is told by the Torah 'she shall be his wife', then surely an אונס (who did an action) must marry her!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא begins to defend the rule by showing that the עשה in the אונס case is extra in the Torah's wording. This sets up his point, which comes next, about what those extra words really teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah tells a מוציא שם רע, who sinned only with words, to keep his wife. An אונס did a real action, so through a קל וחומר he should surely have to marry her too. Since that could be learned on its own, the words 'ולו תהיה לאשה' by אונס must have a different job. That suggests it is not a normal 'preceding' עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who falsely claims his new wife was not a virgin
Let it not be said / the Torah did not need to say
And let us learn it from
All the more so (the closing of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: The question is whether a לאו שקדמו עשה gets lashes. A ברייתא says a ישראל אונס who divorced gets no lashes, which seems to say no. עולא begins to answer by showing that the אונס's עשה ('ולו תהיה לאשה') is extra, since it could be learned through a קל וחומר from מוציא שם רע, so it must be teaching something else.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the עשה of אונס turns out to be a special case, the ברייתא no longer goes against the rule, and רבי יוחנן's original rule can stand.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Let "she shall be his wife" not be stated regarding a rapist,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29. He means the Torah could have left these words out.

phrases.english: and let us learn it from one who defames [his wife]:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה –
phrases.english: If for one who defames, who did no action,
the Torah said "and she shall be his wife,"
then for a rapist, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לוֹ תִּהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה״, בְּאוֹנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the קשיא of step 5 by showing that the אונס's עשה is extra in the Torah's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse differently: showing that the words are extra (a קל וחומר makes them unnecessary), so they must teach something else.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ולו תהיה לאשה' is a normal עשה that comes before the לאו, so the אונס case would go against the rule of לאו שקדמו עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words are extra, since they could be learned through a קל וחומר from מוציא שם רע. This shows the אונס's עשה is not a simple preceding עשה. Step 7 explains what the words teach instead.

steps.title: The extra words teach: if he divorced, he must remarry
steps.stepSummary: עולא finishes his answer. Since 'ולו תהיה לאשה' is not needed for the basic duty to marry, it teaches that if the אונס divorced her, he must take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why does the Torah say it? If it is not needed for the stage before (the first marriage), use it for the stage after: if he divorced her, he must take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא completes his answer from the last step. He shows what the 'extra' words really teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words cannot be wasted. So they are moved from the first marriage to the time after a divorce: he must remarry her. That gives the אונס's לאו ('he may not send her away') an עשה that can fix it after the fact. This explains why a ישראל gets no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it is not needed for this matter.' A rule: when a verse is not needed where it stands, apply it somewhere else.
Before / after. Here it means before the marriage versus after a divorce.
He must take her back (remarry her)

steps.whatToRemember: For an אונס, the עשה of 'ולו תהיה לאשה' really means 'if you divorce her, remarry her.' That is a fixing עשה, so a ישראל gets no lashes.
steps.confusionAlert: In the פסוק, 'ולו תהיה לאשה' is written BEFORE 'לא יוכל לשלחה.' Even so, it works as a fix that comes AFTER the sin of divorcing.

phrases.english: Why is it stated?
phrases.notes: He means the words 'ולו תהיה לאשה' in the אונס section (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: If it is not relevant to the matter before
apply it to the matter after,
that if he divorced, he must take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר? אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְפָנָיו תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's answer that began in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves an extra verse to a new purpose (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אונס's לאו has its עשה before it, so he should get lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עשה really teaches that he must remarry after a divorce. That fixes the לאו, so there are no lashes.

steps.title: You cannot learn אונס from מוציא שם רע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר. A מוציא שם רע is stricter, because he is both lashed and pays, so the אונס cannot be learned from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, you cannot learn the אונס from the מוציא שם רע. It can be refuted: what is special about a מוציא שם רע? He is lashed and also pays!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר that עולא needed to show the words were 'extra.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's whole answer depended on learning the duty to marry for an אונס from the מוציא שם רע. But the מוציא שם רע gets two punishments, lashes and payment. That makes him a harsher case, so his rules may not carry over to the אונס. If the קל וחומר falls, the words are not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute: point out a difference that breaks a comparison
He is lashed AND pays. Two punishments, which is unusual.

phrases.english: But still,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹנֵס מִמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע לָא גָּמַר,
phrases.english: one cannot derive a rapist from a defamer,
because it can be refuted:
what is special about a defamer?
That he is flogged and also pays!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, אוֹנֵס מִמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע לָא גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר that steps 6 and 7 rely on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from מוציא שם רע to אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מוציא שם רע is stricter, since he is lashed and pays, so his law may not apply to the milder אונס.

steps.title: Reverse it: learn מוציא שם רע from אונס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the direction. Learn the duty to marry for a מוציא שם רע from the אונס. Then the extra words in the מוציא שם רע section get moved to the אונס, to teach 'if he divorced, he must remarry.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Torah did not need to write 'she shall be his wife' for the מוציא שם רע. We could learn it from the אונס: if an אונס, who is not lashed and does not pay both, must marry her, then a מוציא שם רע surely must! So why is it written? If it is not needed for the מוציא שם רע, use it for the אונס. If it is not needed for before, use it for after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves עולא's idea by running the קל וחומר the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the stricter case, the מוציא שם רע, is learned from the milder אונס. That works, because if the milder one must marry her, the stricter one surely must. The words in the מוציא שם רע section become extra. They are moved over to the אונס and then to the time after a divorce, teaching that he must remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply it to a different matter

steps.confusionAlert: Here the extra verse is moved twice: first from מוציא שם רע to אונס, and then from 'before' to 'after.'

phrases.english: Rather: let it not say "she shall be his wife"
in the case of the defamer,
and let us derive it from the rapist:
if a rapist, who is not both flogged and paying,
the Merciful One said "and she shall be his wife,"

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then a defamer, is it not all the more so?
So why is it stated?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע –
phrases.english: If it is not relevant to the defamer,
apply it to the rapist;
if it is not relevant to the matter before,
apply it to the matter after.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה״ בְּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, וְלִיגְמַר מֵאוֹנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by reversing the direction of the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the קל וחומר and moves the extra verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The derivation fails because a מוציא שם רע is stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Learn the stricter case from the milder one. The extra words in the מוציא שם רע section then teach the אונס to remarry after a divorce.

steps.title: You cannot learn מוציא שם רע from אונס either
steps.stepSummary: The reversed קל וחומר is also refuted. An אונס is stricter in one way: he did a physical act.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you cannot learn the מוציא שם רע from the אונס either. It can be refuted: what is special about an אונס? He actually did an act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new direction from step 9. Now neither case can be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונס committed a real physical act, while a מוציא שם רע only spoke. So the אונס is harsher in that way, and his rule may not carry over to the מוציא שם רע. Both קל וחומרs fail, so the גמרא still needs another way to show that the words are extra.

keyTerms.meaning: He did an act: a physical deed, not just words

steps.whatToRemember: Each case is stricter in its own way. מוציא שם רע: lashes plus payment. אונס: a physical act. So neither can be learned from the other through a קל וחומר.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע מֵאוֹנֵס נָמֵי לָא גָּמַר,
phrases.english: And one cannot derive a defamer from a rapist either,
because it can be refuted:
what is special about a rapist?
That he performed an action!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע מֵאוֹנֵס נָמֵי לָא גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the reversed קל וחומר from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from אונס to מוציא שם רע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אונס did a physical act, which a מוציא שם רע did not, so the אונס is stricter in that way and the derivation breaks.

steps.title: Moving the extra words from the defamer to the rapist
steps.stepSummary: The words 'ולו תהיה לאשה' in the מוציא שם רע section are not needed, since she is already his wife. So, using 'אם אינו ענין,' they are moved to the אונס, and to the time after he married her: if he divorced, he must remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the Torah did not need to say 'and she shall be his wife' about the defamer, because she is already his wife. So why was it said? If it does not fit the defamer, apply it to the rapist. And if it does not fit the time before the marriage, apply it to the time after.
steps.whatsHappening: After the last קל וחומר fell apart, the גמרא tries a new way to find a source. It uses the extra words in the מוציא שם רע section and moves them to the אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוציא שם רע is already married to the girl, so telling him 'she shall be his wife' adds nothing for him. A rule says that when words have no use in their own place, we move them where they are useful. Here they move to the אונס, and to after the wedding, teaching that if he divorces her, he must take her back.

keyTerms.meaning: If it does not fit [here], a rule for moving extra words of a פסוק to another topic
Before it / after it, meaning before the marriage or after it
Since she is already his wife

phrases.english: Rather: let it not say 'and she shall be his wife'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:19, in the section about the husband who falsely claims his bride was not a virgin.

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ הִיא.
phrases.english: in the case of the defamer, since she is already his wife.
Why was it said?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע
phrases.english: If it does not fit the matter of the defamer,
apply it to the matter of the rapist,
and if it does not fit the time before [the marriage],
phrases.notes: The אונס already has a separate command to marry her the first time, so these words are not needed for that.

phrases.english: apply it to the time after.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא: לא יאמר ולו תהיה לאשה במוציא שם רע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both directions of the קל וחומר were refuted (steps 8 and 10), the גמרא drops the קל וחומר and uses 'אם אינו ענין' instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: moving extra words of a פסוק with 'אם אינו ענין'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed a קל וחומר to link the אונס and the מוציא שם רע, and it failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra words about the מוציא שם רע move straight to the אונס after the marriage, so no קל וחומר is needed.

steps.title: Maybe the extra words stay with the defamer himself
steps.stepSummary: Why move the words to the אונס? Keep them with the מוציא שם רע, but apply them to the time after he married her: if he divorces her, he must remarry and is not lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: if it does not fit the defamer before the marriage, apply it to the defamer's own 'after,' so that he is not lashed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11. The extra words could still be used for the מוציא שם רע himself, so there is no reason to move them to the אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'אם אינו ענין' only moves words to another topic when they truly have no use in their own place. Here they do have a use: the מוציא שם רע himself, after he divorces. Then he must remarry her, so his לאו is fixed by an עשה and he is not lashed. That leaves the אונס without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: But say [instead], introducing another possible reading

phrases.english: But say: and if it does not fit
the time before [the marriage] of the defamer,
apply it to his own time after,
so that he is not lashed!
phrases.notes: Since he can fix the sin by taking her back, it counts as a לאו fixed by an עשה, and there are no lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואימא, ואם אינו ענין לפניו דמוציא שם רע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 11's choice to move the extra words to the אונס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The move of 'ולו תהיה לאשה' from the מוציא שם רע to the אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words still have a use for the מוציא שם רע himself after the marriage, so 'אם אינו ענין' does not allow moving them to a different person.

steps.title: Agreed, and the rapist would be learned from the defamer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge: the words teach about the מוציא שם רע himself. Then the אונס would be learned from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. And the rapist comes and is learned from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the extra words are about the מוציא שם רע. It suggests that the אונס can then be learned from the מוציא שם רע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the step 11 idea alive in a weaker form. The words do not teach about the אונס directly. The אונס would have to be compared to the מוציא שם רע, and that comparison gets tested in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so, agreeing with the challenge
And it comes and is learned from it

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
and the rapist comes and is learned from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אין הכי נמי, ואתי אונס וגמר מיניה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 12 and tries to save the rule for the אונס by comparing him to the מוציא שם רע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing with the challenge, then deriving the case through a comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the words stay with the מוציא שם רע, the אונס has no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אונס can be learned from the מוציא שם רע.

steps.title: Every way of learning the rapist from the defamer can be refuted
steps.stepSummary: How would the אונס be learned from the מוציא שם רע? Whether by קל וחומר or by 'מה מצינו,' the same refutation applies: the מוציא שם רע did no physical act.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what would he be learned from him? Whether by a קל וחומר or by 'what do we find,' it can be refuted the way we refuted it before: what about the defamer? He did not do a physical act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the comparison in step 13 would work. It shows that both possible methods fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ways to learn one case from another are a קל וחומר or 'מה מצינו' (finding the same rule in a similar case). Both fall to the point from step 10: the אונס did a physical act and the מוציא שם רע only spoke. Because the two cases differ, the rule for one cannot be copied to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What do we find,' learning a rule from a similar case
He did not do a physical act

phrases.english: With what would he be learned from him?
Whether by a קל וחומר
or by 'what do we find,'
it can be refuted as we refuted it before:
phrases.notes: This points back to step 10, where the reversed קל וחומר fell apart.

phrases.english: What about the defamer?
He did not do a physical act!

steps.triggerLanguage: במאי גמר מיניה? אי בקל וחומר אי במה מצינו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 13's idea that the אונס can be learned from the מוציא שם רע.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the אונס from the מוציא שם רע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every way of making the comparison fails because the two cases differ: one did a physical act, the other only spoke.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole effort to learn the אונס from the מוציא שם רע fails, by קל וחומר or by מה מצינו. A new source is needed.

steps.title: רבא: 'All his days' means take her back
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new source: 'כל ימיו' in the אונס section teaches that all his days, even after a divorce, he is told 'stand up and take her back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'All his days' means he must stand up and take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier sources failed, רבא gives a new one from the אונס section itself: the words 'כל ימיו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says about the אונס, 'he may not send her away all his days.' רבא reads 'all his days' as a command that lasts forever: even if he divorced her, he must remarry her. That makes his לאו one that is fixed by an עשה, so he is not lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command, which is not punished with lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final source for why an אונס who divorces is not lashed: he can fix the sin by remarrying, as 'כל ימיו' teaches.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
'All his days' — he is under 'stand up and take her back.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא: כל ימיו בעמוד והחזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed sources (steps 6 to 14) with a new source from 'כל ימיו.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source from a different phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed the מוציא שם רע's extra words or a comparison to him, and all of those failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל ימיו' in the אונס section itself teaches that he must remarry her after a divorce.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן taught the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רבין came from ארץ ישראל and reported that רבי יוחנן also said 'כל ימיו' means 'stand up and take her back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: 'All his days' means he must stand up and take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא by showing that רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל taught the very same reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the reasoning. The point is that two separate traditions, רבא in בבל and רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל, agree on 'כל ימיו' as the source, which makes it the accepted answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise, showing agreement from another source
When [a sage] came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: an אונס who divorces his victim must remarry her because of 'כל ימיו.' So his לאו is fixed by an עשה, and he is not lashed. Both רבא and רבי יוחנן agree.

phrases.english: And likewise, when רבין came,
he said that רבי יוחנן said:
'All his days' — he is under 'stand up and take her back.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וכן כי אתא רבין אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רבא's source with the same teaching from רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'כל ימיו' is the source that an אונס who divorces must remarry, which makes his prohibition one fixed by a positive command.

steps.title: רב פפא: This prohibition is not like muzzling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: a לאו that comes together with an extra עשה is not like the לאו of חסימה, the model לאו for lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But its prohibition is not similar to the prohibition of muzzling!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a problem with the rule that one gets lashes for a לאו that comes together with an עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the לאוין that get lashes are learned from the לאו of muzzling an ox (חסימה). That לאו stands alone, with no עשה next to it. So a לאו that has an עשה attached looks different, and maybe it should not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Muzzling an ox while it threshes; the model לאו for lashes

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But its prohibition is not similar
to the prohibition of muzzling!
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4. Every לאו that gets lashes is learned from this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמֵי לָאוֵיהּ לְלָאו דַּחֲסִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אונס source discussion and goes back to the basic rule from step 2, that a לאו שקדמו עשה gets lashes. רב פפא questions that rule against the model לאו of חסימה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule (רבי יוחנן's, upheld by רבא) that one gets lashes for a לאו שקדמו עשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes are learned from חסימה, which has no עשה. A לאו with an עשה is not like it.

steps.title: רבא: An extra מצוה does not make it weaker
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the תורה adding an extra עשה cannot make the לאו weaker, so lashes still apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the Merciful One wrote an extra positive commandment about it, should it become weaker?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב פפא with a question that makes a point: an extra command cannot lighten the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding an עשה makes the matter more serious, not less. It would make no sense for the extra command to take away the lashes. So the difference from חסימה does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One,' meaning ה׳ in His תורה

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because the Merciful One wrote regarding it
an extra positive commandment,
should it be weakened?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתַב בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא עֲשֵׂה יַתִּירָא מִגְרָע גָּרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical argument: an extra stringency cannot reduce punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because it is unlike חסימה, a לאו with an עשה would get no lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: An extra עשה does not weaken the לאו, so lashes still apply

steps.title: Then why no lashes for a לאו הניתק לעשה?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes back: if an extra עשה never weakens a לאו, then a לאו הניתק לעשה should also get lashes, yet it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then for a prohibition that is 'moved over' to a positive commandment, let us also say: because the Merciful One wrote an extra positive commandment about it, should it become weaker?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא uses רבא's own logic against him, pointing to a case where everyone agrees an עשה does remove lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו הניתק לעשה is a לאו that comes with an עשה that fixes it, and there are no lashes for it. By רבא's reasoning, that עשה should not weaken the לאו either. So why does it?

keyTerms.meaning: A לאו that is 'moved over' to an עשה, meaning a מצוה fixes the sin, so there are no lashes

phrases.english: If so,
a prohibition that is 'moved over' to a positive commandment too,
let us say:
because the Merciful One wrote regarding it
an extra positive commandment,
should it be weakened?
phrases.notes: He means: then that לאו should get lashes too, but we know it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לָאו שֶׁנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה נָמֵי, לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's logic that an extra עשה cannot weaken a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A לאו הניתק לעשה has an extra עשה and gets no lashes, which contradicts רבא's logic.

steps.title: רבא: That עשה comes to detach the לאו
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in a לאו הניתק לעשה, the עשה comes on purpose to detach the לאו from lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That one comes in order to detach the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא separates the two cases: an extra עשה that only adds, and an עשה whose job is to fix the לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the עשה gives a way to fix the sin, its purpose is to replace lashes with that fix. When the עשה is just extra, as in the case of the לאו with an עשה, it does not take away lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: To detach, to cut off (the לאו from lashes)

steps.whatToRemember: An extra עשה does not cancel lashes. Only an עשה that comes to fix the לאו (לאו הניתק לעשה) removes lashes.

phrases.english: He said to him:
That one, to detach the prohibition
is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְנַתּוֹקֵי לָאו הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's pushback and closes the side question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between an extra עשה and an עשה that comes to fix the לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any עשה connected to a לאו should be treated the same way
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an עשה whose purpose is to fix the לאו removes lashes

steps.title: Does 'כל ימיו' work under 'קיימו ולא קיימו'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's 'כל ימיו' answer. It works for the view of ביטלו ולא ביטלו, but what about the view of קיימו ולא קיימו?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says 'he cancelled it or did not cancel it,' but according to the one who says 'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it,' what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבא's answer about the אונס and asks whether it holds up under both opinions about לאו הניתק לעשה. It first sets up the opinion where the answer works, then asks about the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under 'ביטלו ולא ביטלו', a person gets lashes only once the מצוה can no longer be done. Since the אונס can always remarry, he is never lashed. Under 'קיימו ולא קיימו', he gets lashes as soon as he fails to do the מצוה right away, so 'כל ימיו' should not save him.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (setup before a question)
View that lashes depend on whether he made the מצוה impossible
View that lashes depend on whether he did the מצוה right away

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree on the basic idea of לאו הניתק לעשה. They argue only about the point at which the chance to fix the sin is over and lashes apply.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
phrases.notes: 'This' is רבא's answer from before: the אונס is told all his days to take her back.

phrases.english: 'he cancelled it or did not cancel it,'
but according to the one who says
'he fulfilled it or did not fulfill it,'
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בִּיטְּלוֹ וְלֹא בִּיטְּלוֹ, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question and goes back to רבא's 'כל ימיו' answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the אונס gets no lashes because he can always remarry her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under 'קיימו ולא קיימו', failing to remarry right away already brings lashes, so the lifelong chance to remarry does not prevent them.
